content.title: BIGBANG’s Blistering Coachella Setlist And Review
content.text: BIGBANG open their debut Coachella set. coachella/YouTubeKPop veterans BIGBANG, known popularly as the ‘Kings of KPop’, took the stage for their long awaited Coachella debut on Sunday. Now a trio of G-Dragon, Taeyang, and Daesung, the long-running group was the Outdoor Theatre’s final act of the night, following Laufey. BIGBANG’s Coachella Setlist Was Full of Familiar BangersBIGBANG during their debut Coachella performancecoachella/YouTubeThe show opened with “Bang Bang Bang,” with screams heard on the livestream from the first iconic notes of the intro. From there the set moved through a medley that included "Fantastic Baby," and "Sober," before moving on to “Loser” and 2006’s “A Fool Of Tears”, a sweep of their catalogue that covered multiple eras and reminded a mixed audience of just how many canonical songs they have."Haru Haru" drew lightsticks throughout the crowd, which included BLACKPINK members and former labelmates Rosé and Lisa. "Lies" got some of the biggest screams of the night. Between the high intensity group moments, the set made room for individual spotlights.In a bit of real Korean representation, Daesung brought trot music to Coachella for the very first time with his trot song "Hando Chogua," pausing at the end to ask the audience, in genuine disbelief, how they knew it. We’re probably getting He followed it up with "Look at Me Gwisun." BIGBANG member Daesung performs trot song 'Hando Chogua' at Coachellacoachella/YouTubeTaeyang took his solo moment with "Ringa Linga." Then came one of the night's most theatrical sequences: G-Dragon making his way to the stage from the floor, building anticipation before launching into his solo material, including "Power" and a GD x Taeyang collaboration "Good Boy." The band behind them was, by multiple accounts, a superlative The Band Six (love to see black excellence!). The bass line arriving before "Lies" set off its own reaction.A costume change (the third of the night) preceded "Bad Boy," followed by “We Like to Party.”The Band Six tears it up accompanying BIGBANG on their Coachella debut.coachella/YouTubeWhy This Moment Mattered For BIGBANGTo understand the weight of Friday’s performance, it helps to know how close it came to not happening.BIGBANG debuted on August 19, 2006 under YG Entertainment, with a formation documented on MTV Korea that drew over a million online viewers before the group had released their first commercial track. Even though this is more common now, at the time, they built their career from there into something the KPop industry had not produced before: a self-writing, self-producing boy group whose music crossed genres freely, whose members had as much individual identity as collective force, and whose commercial footprint stretched from South Korea to Japan to China to the West. BELFAST, NORTHERN IRELAND - NOVEMBER 06: (EXCLUSIVE COVERAGE) Seungri, G-Dragon, Taeyang, T.O.P, Daesung of Korean boy band Big Bang pose with their Worldwide Act award backstage during the MTV Europe Music Awards 2011 at Odyssey Arena on November 6, 2011 in Belfast, Northern Ireland. (Photo by Dave Hogan/MTV 2011/Getty Images)Getty ImagesIn 2016, Forbes listed the group at number 23 on its list of the world’s highest paid musicians, having earned $44 million in a single year — the first Korean act on the list, with the third highest annual earnings ever for a boy band, behind only One Direction and Backstreet Boys. That same year, Time magazine's reader poll ranked them second on its Most Influential People in the World list, behind only Bernie Sanders.Then came the losses. In 2019, member Seungri retired from the entertainment industry following his involvement in the Burning Sun scandal. SEOUL, SOUTH KOREA - MARCH 14: Seungri, formerly a member of South Korean boy band BIGBANG is seen arriving at a Seoul police station on March 14, 2019 in Seoul, South Korea. Seungri of South Korean boy band BIGBANG appeared at the police station on Thursday to be questioned over the charges of supplying prostitution services. (Photo by Han Myung-Gu/WireImage)WireImageIn 2022, the group returned as a quartet with “Still Life”, their first release in four years, which debuted at number one on South Korea's Gaon Digital Chart and entered the top 10 on the Billboard Global 200. A year later, T.O.P publicly confirmed his departure from the group. By 2023, BIGBANG was three.The Coachella booking, announced as part of a 2026 world tour marking their 20th anniversary, carried the additional meaning of a long-deferred promise. BIGBANG had already been confirmed for Coachella 2020 before COVID cancelled that edition entirely. Friday night was the fulfilment of that invitation, six years late and with a smaller lineup, but no less loudly received.What BIGBANG Said At CoachellaMassive crowds at BIGBANG's debut Coachella set. coachella/YouTubeTaeyang addressed the crowd with the context that made the night what it was. "2026 is our 20th year as BIGBANG. The years have flown by so fast. We already spent half our lives together and I'm so grateful to share our music and our passion with all of you. This stage tonight — Coachella — means a lot to us." He also shouted out his new solo album and the VIPS, the group's fanbase.Daesung followed: "This has become an unforgettable memory for me and we're gonna make even more unforgettable memories this year so stay with us till the end."G-Dragon, characteristically, just cheekily said “ok bye bye,” but then walked it back. “I just really want to say thank you, thank you, thank you,” he said. "This year is BIGBANG’s 20th anniversary, it just started. We got some biiiiiig things coming soon. So, for now, for just a little bit, stay there, we'll be there."Taeyang also thanked their Korean fans in Korean before the final song.Still Life — And TOP's VerseThe BIGBANG members hug closing out their debut Coachella set.coachella/YouTubeThe trio, all aged between 36 and 38, closed out the set with "Still Life," the 2022 single that served as BIGBANG’s first release in four years and the last to feature former member T.O.P before his departure. The group left T.O.P’s verse in.The song debuted at number one on South Korea’s Gaon Digital Chart and reached the top 10 on the Billboard Global 200 — the third KPop group to do so since the chart launched in 2020. At the end, G-Dragon, Taeyang, and Daesung hugged on stage, an emotional finale to a set years in the making, in front of a massive crowd cheering for a group whose last album was a decade ago.Why 20 Years Is Rare in KPopDaesung, Taeyang and GDragon of BIGBANG close out their debut Coachella set. coachella/YouTubeTwo decades is an almost anomalous achievement in an industry whose average group lifespan is estimated at around seven years. The KPop system is built for intensity and turnover: exhausting promotion cycles, complex choreography, tightly managed contracts, and an audience that moves quickly from one generation of stars to the next. Most groups disband long before their tenth anniversary.The handful of acts that have made it to twenty years have done so through some combination of loyal fanbases, artistic reinvention, and — not to be underestimated — surviving the mandatory military service that removes Korean male artists from public view for roughly two years each. Super Junior, who debuted in 2005, wrapped up their 20th anniversary world tour in April 2026. TVXQ held a three-day performance at Tokyo Dome in April 2025 to mark their own 20th anniversary. Shinhwa, who debuted in 1998, is the longest-running KPop group that is still active, notable for having maintained the same lineup throughout. BIGBANG now joins that short list, albeit as a reduced lineup.20 years together is a long time for any act. For many groups, it involves, like Taeyang said, spending (sometimes more than) “half their lives” together. And for a group that helped architect the global KPop industry, whose fingerprints are on the sound, the fashion, and the ambition of nearly every group that followed, Coachella is the perfect scale to be kicking off celebrations.BIGBANG’s Full Setlist at Coachella Weekend 1Bang Bang BangFantastic Baby (medley)Sober (medley)LoserA Fool of TearsHaru HaruLiesRinga Linga (Taeyang solo)Power (G-Dragon solo)Good Boy (GD x Taeyang)Hando Chogua (Daesung solo)Look at Me Gwisun (Daesung solo)Home Sweet Home (G-Dragon feat. Taeyang & Daesung)Bad BoyWe Like to PartyStill LifeBIGBANG will perform again at Coachella Weekend 2 on April 17.
